item.title: Iran pursues cautious escalation ahead of US midterms
item.description: Tehran appears to be boosting pressure on Washington ahead of the crucial midterm vote, but shows little desire to return to a full-scale war.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: India's BRICS strategy tested with Xi, Putin set to visit
item.description: New Delhi's "America Plus" approach sees India deepening its ties with China and Russia, while also trying to keep BRICS from turning into an anti-Western platform.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Uber leaves two key African markets — and their drivers in despair
item.description: Uber's departure from Nigeria and Uganda has left countless customers high and dry. But what about drivers? With fuel prices, maintenance and other operating costs rising, many say they're struggling to make a living.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Iran war: Saudi-Houthi escalation intensifies Yemen conflict
item.description: The Houthi takeovers of Mokha, Dhubab and Perim in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait threaten to push Yemen deeper into the Middle East war. The Iran-backed group has made advances against Yemen's government and Saudi Arabia.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Why North Korea's Kim Jong Un doesn't need a US deal
item.description: Donald Trump's overtures to North Korea's dictator have gone nowhere, with an emboldened Pyongyang accelerating its nuclear program and solidifying alliances with Russia and China.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Turks in Germany anxious after AfD wins in Saxony-Anhalt
item.description: The Alternative for Germany party's win in Saxony-Anhalt has alarmed people of Turkish origin in eastern states. Will workers and business owners abandon the increasingly AfD-friendly region for the more welcoming west?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Hong Kong Tiananmen activists jailed for up to 7 years
item.description: Three pro-democracy activists who organized annual commemorations of China's deadly 1989 Tiananmen crackdown were charged under Hong Kong's Beijing-backed national security law.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Magyar vs. Moscow: Hungary toughens stance toward Russia
item.description: Prime Minister Peter Magyar has abruptly ended the era of his predecessor's warm relations with Russia: Hungary has expelled 10 Russian diplomats. The Kremlin is considering halting gas supplies in response.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Philippines ferry fire: Search continues for dozens missing
item.description: Firefighters searching for survivors combed through the smoking remains of a ferry off the coast of Coron island in the Philippines. Dozens of people have died, and more than 40 have been rescued.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Germany's connection to the 9/11 attacks
item.description: The 9/11 plot, including the twin tower attacks, was partly planned by the so-called Hamburg cell. A look at how Germany's national security was reshaped.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Digital data leeches: Trading on our profiles
item.description: US tech companies gather, link, and sell more and more information about their users. The scandal involving the dating app Grindr shows how easy it is for highly sensitive data to fall into the wrong hands.
item.dc:subject: World
